rendered: The review starts from the total known global cobalt reserves, taken from the United States Geological Survey report on cobalt: (7 million metric tons)[1] It then applies reduction steps stated in the text. First, it assumes a conservative mining efficiency: ≈70% yearly mining efficiency[2]. Next, it assumes only a share of the mined cobalt goes to battery makers: ≈40% of the mined cobalt directed toward battery manufacturing[3]. Applying these factors to the reserves gives the cobalt usable for batteries: ≈2 million metric tons globally[4]. The model in Figure 1c[5] plots this usable reserve as the "Total Cobalt Available for Battery Manufacturing" against the rising cobalt requirement, and the review concludes that demand will exceed that supply before 2045[6], with the cobalt deficit shown as the shaded region at the right of the plot.
